summary: idnna typosquats idna and drops an opaque binary from a personal GitHub release at install time
details: The package name 'idnna' resembles the widely used 'idna' library, while its internal setup identifies as 'requestss'. setup.py registers a custom install cmdclass (LinuxInstall) whose run() method decodes a base64-obfuscated hook (_HOOK_B64) and executes it via exec(compile(...)). On Linux hosts, the decoded hook uses urllib.urlretrieve to fetch an unversioned, opaque binary from https://github.com/totti2188/8gp1Q7iZD3h4VW/releases/download/v1.3A/something into /tmp/something, chmods it 0755, and launches it detached in the background via subprocess.Popen with start_new_session=True. The setup() name is parameterized through the PYPI_PACKAGE_NAME environment variable, enabling one source tree to be published under multiple typosquat names. The fetched binary is from a personal GitHub account unrelated to any published 'idna' or 'requests' maintainer, is not pinned by hash or signature, and is executed with no integrity verification.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
